entries.label: Discord
entries.reads: Read channels, messages, threads, and members in the servers your bot was invited to.
entries.sends: Send messages and reactions as your bot, after you approve each one. Read only hides them.

fields.label: Bot token (from the Bot page of your Discord application)

steps: Open the Discord Developer Portal and choose New Application. Give it a name, for example Abito.
Open the Bot page and choose Reset Token. Copy the token and keep it for the last step.
On the same page, under Privileged Gateway Intents, turn on Message Content Intent and Server Members Intent, then save.
Open OAuth2, then URL Generator. Check the scope bot, then the permissions View Channels, Read Message History, Send Messages, Send Messages in Threads, and Add Reactions.
Open the generated address, pick your server, and choose Authorize. The bot can only see the servers you invite it to.
Choose Continue here and paste the bot token. It stays on this computer, in the secure store.
guide.note: This uses a community server, not one made by Discord. Your bot acts in Discord with the permissions you gave it.

entries.label: Slack
entries.reads: Search messages, channels, and people, and read channels, threads, and canvases.
entries.sends: Send and schedule messages as you, after you approve each one. Read only hides them.

fields.label: Client Secret (leave it empty if your app uses PKCE)

steps: Open Slack's app page and choose Create New App, then From scratch. Pick your workspace.
Open OAuth & Permissions. Under Redirect URLs, add http://localhost:38417/callback and save it.
On the same page, turn on PKCE (Slack only accepts a redirect to this computer with it).
Under User Token Scopes, add the search, history, read and chat:write scopes the guide lists.
Open Basic Information and copy the Client ID (and the Client Secret, if you want to use it).
Choose Continue here, paste them, and approve access in the page that opens.
guide.note: Your workspace admin may need to approve the app. OAuth sign-in itself is not implemented yet: the client settings are sealed for a later unit.

entries.label: Gmail
entries.reads: Search and read your email threads, drafts, and labels.
entries.sends: Draft and send mail as you, after you approve each one. Read only hides them.

steps: In the Google Cloud console, create a project (or pick one of yours).
Enable the Gmail API and the Gmail MCP API for that project.
Open Google Auth Platform, then Branding, and choose Get Started. Name the app, pick your email, choose External (or Internal for a Workspace), and finish.
Open Audience and add your own address as a test user. Open Data Access and add the scopes gmail.readonly and gmail.compose.
Open Clients, choose Create Client, then Web application. Add http://localhost:38418/callback as an Authorized redirect URI, create it, and copy the Client ID and the Client Secret.
Choose Continue here, paste them, and approve access in the page that opens.
guide.note: Gmail's server is a Developer Preview: your account must be in the Google Workspace Developer Preview Program. OAuth sign-in itself is not implemented yet: the client settings are sealed for a later unit.
